name: Release close-out gate — internal version-consistency mechanization

design_notes.plan_ref: definition-of-done-stateful-kettle.md F-097 ("release close-out gate") -- the sole scope-of-record for this contract's script, workflow, release.yml wiring, and assertion list. This feature is a DAG root (no dependencies) and may proceed in parallel with feature 093; it does not depend on, and does not read or write, any 09x-prefixed feature's contract or QA artifact other than its own.
design_notes.what_this_feature_is: Mechanizes internal version-anchor consistency across the release surface via a stdlib-only, network-free close-out script with two modes (--mode pr for internal consistency; --mode tag for tag-vs-CHANGELOG consistency), wired as a paths-filtered pull-request workflow (self-triggers on this very phase's PR since every feature touches CHANGELOG.md) and as one new blocking step in release.yml between tag resolution and publication. Generalizes the require(label, condition) assertion style already proven in .agent/evidence/091/verify_release_prep.py. Lives under .github/, not tools/, per release.yml's own header doctrine: tools/ is bootstrap-injected consumer payload, and release publication is framework-envelope-only concern.
design_notes.release_yml_anchor_step: The new tag-mode step is inserted immediately AFTER the existing 'Resolve and verify the tag' step (id: tag, .github/workflows/release.yml lines 49-101, which validates the vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag shape, verifies the tag exists, and resolves the annotated-tag title) and immediately BEFORE the existing 'Extract the tag's CHANGELOG section' step (lines 102-129, which awk-extracts the '## [VERSION]' block that becomes the Release notes and is consumed by the final 'Create or update the GitHub Release' step at line 130). This ordering is load-bearing: the new step reads steps.tag.outputs.tag (produced by the anchor step) and must fail the job before CHANGELOG.md is read for publication, so a version-inconsistent tree can never reach 'Create or update the GitHub Release'.
design_notes.hand_walk_pr_mode_against_current_tree: Independently hand-walked every PR-mode assertion against the current tree (base_revision ecfc4ee, V = NIZAM.json framework.version = "1.0.0", read at NIZAM.json line 4) before writing this contract, since the script cannot be executed pre-implementation: (1) CONTEXT.md frontmatter 'version: 1.0.0' (line 5) == V, and change_log[0].version == "1.0.0" == V -- PASS. (2) docs/guide/index.html carries '' (line 6) == V and '1.0.0' (line 665, re-derived via grep -n; round-0 mis-cited this as line 664) == V -- PASS. (3) README.md pins agree with V: 'raw.githubusercontent.com/niq-cnr/nizam-framework/v1.0.0/bootstrap.sh' (line 22, re-derived; round-0 mis-cited line 20), 'GOVERNANCE_TAG=v1.0.0' (line 24, re-derived; round-0 mis-cited line 21) and '--tag v1.0.0' (also line 24, the same line as GOVERNANCE_TAG), 'releases/tag/v1.0.0' (line 44, re-derived; round-0 mis-cited line 40) -- PASS; the 'docs/migration-v1.0.0.md' link is on line 45 (re-derived) -- a DIFFERENT line from the releases-tag pin at line 44, correcting round-0's false 'same line' claim -- and is deliberately EXCLUDED from the assertion set regardless of line position (see migration_link_exclusion_rationale below). (4) CHANGELOG.md: the first '## [' heading strictly after '## [Unreleased]' (line 8) is '## [1.0.0] - 2026-08-15' (line 27), a literal starts-with match against '## [1.0.0] - ' (WITH the trailing space-hyphen-space, the single awk-compatible prefix form this contract now states once, unambiguously -- see assertion_summary_pr_mode item 4) -- PASS; that section's first content line (line 29) reads '**Major release** (`methodology/06_release_train.md` §3.1): ...' -- the tier-banner-plus-citation assertion PASSES. (5) docs/planning/ROADMAP.md: grep -c 'Latest released tag: v1.0.0\|Release in preparation: v1.0.0', RESTRICTED TO THE DOCUMENT BODY (lines strictly after the closing frontmatter '---' at line 120 -- see assertion_summary_pr_mode item 5 for the body-only rationale), returns exactly 1 (line 617: 'Latest released tag: v1.0.0 (MAJOR) -- RELEASED 2026-08-15.'), and there is no 'Release in preparation: v1.0.0' line in the body on the current tree -- PASS. All five PR-mode assertion groups hand-walk to PASS on the current tree, so `python3 .github/scripts/release_closeout.py --mode pr` MUST exit 0 once implemented, without requiring any version-anchor edit as part of this contract (F-098 owns the next bump, to 1.1.0, after which the same five groups must re-hand-walk to PASS at V=1.1.0 -- the evergreen-invariant property recorded in the plan).
design_notes.evergreen_invariant_rationale: The five-group PR-mode invariant holds identically whether every anchor reads 1.0.0 (now, mid-phase) or 1.1.0 (after F-098's release-prep bump): the script always compares every anchor against the single NIZAM.json reference, never against a literal version string baked into the script. Because every phase-013 feature's contract touches CHANGELOG.md, the paths-filtered PR workflow self-pilots on this very phase's own pull request -- it will run, and must pass, on the phase-013 PR itself once feature 098 completes the bump.
design_notes.migration_link_exclusion_rationale: docs/migration-v1.0.0.md is deliberately NOT part of the README pin-agreement assertion group: unlike the curl URL / GOVERNANCE_TAG / --tag / releases-tag pins (which all name the CURRENT release), the migration-guide link names the latest MIGRATION, which by design stays pinned to v1.0.0 (the last release that required a migration guide) even after a MINOR bump to v1.1.0 with no new migration guide -- F-098's plan text states this explicitly ('migration link stays v1.0.0 -- no new migration guide on MINOR'). Asserting migration-link==V would make the PR-mode gate FAIL on every no-new-migration release, which is the common case, so it is excluded by design and the rationale is recorded here so a future reader does not silently 'fix' this as an oversight.
design_notes.tag_mode_additions: In --mode tag --tag vX.Y.Z, the script runs every PR-mode assertion group PLUS three more: (a) the supplied tag matches the anchored regex ^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ (identical semver-tag shape already enforced inline in release.yml's own 'Resolve and verify the tag' step, so the close-out script re-validates rather than trusts the caller); (b) the supplied tag, minus its leading 'v', equals V (NIZAM.json framework.version) exactly -- catching a tag pushed against a tree whose anchors were never bumped; (c) CHANGELOG.md's top released section (the same 'first heading after Unreleased' located in PR-mode assertion group 4) names that same version -- catching a CHANGELOG edited out of lockstep with the tag. CORRECTED MECHANISM (round-1 revision, fixing MAJOR finding I2): tag mode does NOT trust the ambient checkout for any anchor. Every one of the six PR-mode anchor files (NIZAM.json, CONTEXT.md, docs/guide/index.html, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/planning/ROADMAP.md) is instead read via `git show "$TAG:<path>"`, mirroring release.yml's own extraction-step discipline verbatim: `VERSION="${TAG#v}"` (release.yml line 107) followed immediately by `git show "$TAG:CHANGELOG.md" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/CHANGELOG.at-tag.md"` (release.yml line 111, comment at lines 108-110 stating this reads CHANGELOG.md 'AS IT EXISTS AT THE TAG ... so re-publishing an old tag reproduces that release's own record'). The round-0 ambient-checkout design broke release.yml's own documented workflow_dispatch republish path: release.yml lines 20-27 state 'workflow_dispatch exists for tags cut before this workflow landed ... or for re-publishing corrected notes for an existing tag', and on that trigger `github.ref` is the default branch, not the tag -- so ambient-checkout anchors would silently compare against HEAD-of-branch content instead of the tag's own content, defeating the whole point of a tag-mode gate. No change to release.yml's checkout step is required to support the git-show mechanism: it already runs with `fetch-depth: 0` (release.yml line 46, inside the `actions/checkout` step at line 40, whose own comment at lines 42-45 states this is load-bearing precisely so 'a dispatch-supplied tag ref resolves' via a full tag fetch) -- confirmed sufficient because `git show "$TAG:<path>"` only needs the tag's object graph present locally, not a working-tree checkout of that ref, which is exactly what release.yml's own extraction step already relies on at line 111. release_closeout.py's --mode tag therefore shells out to `git show` (read-only, ref-non-mutating) once per anchor file instead of opening those files directly from disk; --mode pr is unaffected and continues to read the ambient working tree directly. Round-2 revision (fixing MAJOR finding I7): reading via `git show` restores exact-content-at-tag fidelity for every anchor unconditionally (the MAJOR I2 fix) -- but fidelity alone does not guarantee `--mode tag` exits 0 for every historical tag; see tag_mode_era_safety_design for the full (a)/(b)/(a-extension) mechanism and the verified, evidence-narrower outcome hand-walked across all 14 existing tags: rules (a)/(b) are crash-free for every file-level-absence and ROADMAP pre-convention gap across all 14 tags, the (a)-extension sub-anchor-absence path is also crash-free but deliberately emits a named FAIL rather than a SKIP, and the resulting FAIL set is the eleven tags v0.1.0 through v0.7.0 (v0.1.0 under its own distinct pre-convention cause; v0.2.0 through v0.7.0 for value drift plus tier-banner absence) -- a majority, not a minority, of the 14 tags -- which this contract's non_goals (the dedicated value-drift-republication entry added in round-3) explicitly do not authorize repairing.
design_notes.no_self_tag_design: release_closeout.py performs only string/regex comparison against version anchors and the tag string it is handed as a CLI argument; it never invokes `git tag`, `git push`, or any subprocess that mutates refs. In --mode pr it reads every anchor directly from the working tree (no subprocess at all). In --mode tag (round-1 revision, per the tag_mode_additions fix for MAJOR finding I2) it shells out to `git show "$TAG:<path>"` once per anchor file (NIZAM.json, CONTEXT.md, docs/guide/index.html, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/planning/ROADMAP.md) -- a read-only, ref-non-mutating subprocess call, distinct in kind from `git tag`/`git push` -- plus, optionally, a pure-regex tag-shape check requiring no subprocess. This remains grep-asserted in verification (no `git (tag|push)` token anywhere in the file; `git show` matches neither the `tag` nor the `push` pattern) and is still the mechanized form of product_spec_013.md's 'the pipeline never self-tags' safety invariant and this contract's own non_goals entry below.
design_notes.assertion_summary_pr_mode: (1) CONTEXT.md frontmatter version == V AND change_log[0].version == V. (2) docs/guide/index.html framework-version meta == V AND footer-version span == V. (3) README.md curl URL / GOVERNANCE_TAG / --tag / releases-tag pins all == V (migration link excluded, rationale above). (4) CHANGELOG.md first '## [' heading after '## [Unreleased]' is literal-starts-with '## [V] - ' (YYYY-MM-DD suffix, not asserted beyond presence of a heading match) AND that section's body contains one of '**Major release**' / '**Minor release**' / '**Patch release**' AND the substring 'methodology/06_release_train.md'. (5) ROADMAP.md names vV in exactly one of 'Latest released tag: vV' or 'Release in preparation: vV' (grep -c over both patterns combined == 1), SCOPED TO THE DOCUMENT BODY ONLY -- lines strictly after the closing frontmatter '---' delimiter (ROADMAP.md's frontmatter opens at line 1 and closes at line 120 on the current tree) -- because the YAML frontmatter's change_log array is a running history of prose summaries that may legitimately narrate a PAST disposition using the same literal phrase for an earlier version (house precedent: ROADMAP.md line 32's phase-013-proposal change_log summary contains the literal substring 'Release in preparation: v0.9.0', narrating the prior release cycle, not the current one); a frontmatter-inclusive grep could therefore return a count > 1, or match a stale version's disposition, purely from historical narration -- breaking the 'exactly one disposition' invariant for reasons unrelated to the current release state (Advisory finding (a), round-1 revision).
design_notes.assertion_summary_tag_mode: All five PR-mode groups, each evaluated by reading its anchor file's content via `git show "$TAG:<path>"` rather than the ambient checkout (round-1 revision, fixing MAJOR finding I2 -- see tag_mode_additions for the full mechanism and rationale), each SKIPPING (not crashing, not FAILing) when its own anchor file is absent at the tag, and group 5 additionally SKIPPING when neither disposition label names the tag's own version anywhere in the at-tag document body (round-2 revision, fixing MAJOR finding I7 -- see tag_mode_era_safety_design for the full (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) mechanism, rationale, and the verified per-tag outcome across all 14 existing tags), PLUS: tag shape regex; tag-stripped-of-v == V; CHANGELOG top released section version == tag-stripped-of-v (also read via `git show "$TAG:CHANGELOG.md"`). The absence/pre-convention SKIP rules (a)/(b), and the sub-anchor-absence named-FAIL path ((a)-extension in tag_mode_era_safety_design), do not, and are not intended to, suppress the genuine anchor VALUE mismatches carried by the ten historical tags v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.6.0, v0.7.0 (the class (i)/(ii)/(iii) hand-walk in tag_mode_era_safety_design sub-rule (d), class (iii) being the tier-banner sub-anchor-absence FAIL that applies to all ten of these tags in addition to whichever of (i)/(ii) each also carries); those tags correctly continue to FAIL, v0.1.0 additionally and separately joins the intentionally-blocked list under its own distinct pre-convention cause (CONTEXT.md present with no change_log key, README.md present with no version pins, CHANGELOG.md's [0.1.0] section present with no tier banner -- none of classes (i)/(ii)/(iii), since v0.1.0 carries no NIZAM.json/CONTEXT.md value drift at all), and this contract's non_goals (round-4 revision) now states explicitly that repairing any of these eleven tags is out of scope, so the verified republishable set under --mode tag is v0.8.0, v0.9.0, v1.0.0, and every future tag (three historical tags, not four).
design_notes.generalization_of_091_precedent: require(label: str, condition: bool) -> None mirrors .agent/evidence/091/verify_release_prep.py's function verbatim (raise AssertionError(label) on failure, print(f"PASS {label}") on success), generalized here to ALSO print 'FAIL <label>' and sys.exit(1) at the first failure instead of letting a Python traceback surface, per the plan's 'require(label, cond) style printing PASS <label> per assertion, first failure prints FAIL <label> and exits 1' wording -- a CLI-usable hardening of the evidence-script-only precedent, since this script runs unattended in CI rather than being read by a human alongside its evidence capture.
design_notes.tag_mode_era_safety_design: Round-2 revision, fixing MAJOR finding I7: --mode tag is era-safe BY CONSTRUCTION, mirroring C16's doctrine that presence is the declaration and no cutoff dates are hard-coded anywhere in the check. (a) ANCHOR-ABSENCE SKIP: for each of the six anchor files (see tag_mode_additions), if `git show "$TAG:<path>"` exits non-zero (the file does not exist at that tag), that anchor's assertion group SKIPS -- printing an explicit `PASS <group-label> (skipped: <path> absent at <tag>)` line -- instead of crashing (an uncaught non-zero git-show propagating to a Python exception, effectively exit 2) or FAILing (which would wrongly treat 'the convention did not exist yet at this tag' as 'the convention was violated'). (a-EXT) SUB-ANCHOR-ABSENCE NAMED FAIL (round-4 revision, fixing MAJOR finding I10): rule (a)'s SKIP is strictly FILE-LEVEL -- it fires only when `git show "$TAG:<path>"` itself exits non-zero. When the file EXISTS at the tag but an expected anchor WITHIN it is absent (CONTEXT.md present with no `change_log` key; README.md present with none of its four pins; a CHANGELOG.md release section present with no tier-banner line), rule (a) does NOT apply and this is a categorically different disposition: the script emits a named `FAIL <label> (anchor absent in <path> at <tag>)` for that specific assertion group -- never an uncaught exception (which would otherwise surface as an unhandled Python exception, effectively exit 2) and never a silent SKIP -- and proceeds through the same first-failure exit-1 path as any other genuine FAIL, because a present-but-incomplete file is real, reportable evidence that the tag predates that anchor's own introduction within an already-adopted file, not a condition the gate should paper over. (b) ROADMAP DISPOSITION SKIP (group 5 at-tag): the body-scoped count is parameterized by the TAG's own version, not V -- `grep -c` over 'Latest released tag: v<TAG-version>' or 'Release in preparation: v<TAG-version>', restricted to the document body (lines strictly after the at-tag frontmatter's closing '---', mirroring assertion_summary_pr_mode item 5's body-only rationale; the frontmatter-close line itself is recomputed per tag since it shifts release-to-release -- confirmed by hand-walk at line 111 (v1.0.0), line 102 (v0.9.0), line 36 (v0.8.0), line 12 (v0.6.0)). If that tag-version-scoped count is 0, the group SKIPS with an explicit `PASS ROADMAP disposition (skipped: pre-convention ROADMAP at <tag>)` line -- this covers both the true pre-convention case and the case where only a STALE prior-version disposition line survives in the body (e.g. v0.8.0's body carries only 'Latest released tag: v0.7.0', never a v0.8.0 line, because the ROADMAP disposition edit that names v0.8.0 lands in a later, separate post-release-refresh commit, not the tag's own commit). If the count is >= 1, the group asserts count == 1 exactly, the same exactly-one invariant PR mode already enforces, just tag-version-parameterized instead of V-parameterized. (c) COMPENSATING CONTROL: this leniency is safe going forward because the FORWARD-LOOKING enforcement of the disposition line already lives in --mode pr (assertion_summary_pr_mode item 5 is unconditional on the CURRENT tree -- no skip logic exists in PR mode at all): every PR that lands must carry its own phase's ROADMAP disposition edit and PR mode strictly requires exactly one match against the CURRENT V before that PR can merge, so the invariant is enforced at merge time, before a tag is ever cut. --mode tag's group-5 leniency therefore only ever applies to REPUBLISHING a tag whose commit predates that PR-time enforcement (or predates the ROADMAP-disposition convention entirely) -- it never weakens enforcement on a fresh tag. (d) VERIFIED OUTCOME -- hand-walked via `git show "$TAG:<path>"` probes across ALL 14 existing tags (v0.1.0 through v1.0.0), not merely the two tags named in the finding: rule (a) fires correctly for group 2 (docs/guide/index.html, absent at v0.1.0/v0.2.0) and group 5 (docs/planning/ROADMAP.md, absent at v0.1.0 through v0.5.3); rule (b) fires correctly at v0.6.0 (body count 0; the surviving label reads only 'v0.5.3'), v0.7.0 (body count 0), and v0.8.0 (body count 0; the surviving label reads only 'v0.7.0'), and correctly does NOT skip at v0.9.0 / v1.0.0 (body count 1, the tag's own 'Release in preparation: v<ver>' line). CORRECTION TO THE ROUND-1/FINDING-I7 ASSUMPTION THAT PROMPTED THIS FIX: rules (a)+(b) alone do NOT make `--mode tag` exit 0 for every one of the 14 tags -- the comprehensive sweep surfaced THREE DISTINCT, PRE-EXISTING anchor-inconsistency classes, none an absence and none within this contract's non_goals-authorized repair scope: (i) NIZAM.json framework.version itself lags the tag string at v0.2.0 (reads 0.1.0), v0.5.2 and v0.5.3 (both read 0.5.1) -- so tag-mode additions (b) tag-stripped-of-v==V and (c) CHANGELOG-top==tag genuinely and correctly FAIL at those three tags; (ii) CONTEXT.md's own frontmatter 'version:' field functioned as an independently-evolving document-revision counter, NOT tracking NIZAM.json's framework.version, for seven tags v0.3.0 through v0.7.0 (e.g. at the v0.6.0 tag, NIZAM.json reads 0.6.0 while CONTEXT.md reads 0.5.0) until the two converged starting at v0.8.0 -- so PR-mode group 1 (mirrored verbatim into tag mode) genuinely and correctly FAILS at those seven tags; (iii) the CHANGELOG.md tier-banner sub-assertion within PR-mode group 4 (assertion_summary_pr_mode item 4's '**Major release**' / '**Minor release**' / '**Patch release**' substring check), reached via the sub-anchor-absence named-FAIL path (see the (a)-extension above, since the [VERSION] section is itself present at every one of these tags -- only its tier-banner line is missing), genuinely and correctly FAILS at ALL TEN of v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.6.0, v0.7.0, because the tier-banner convention itself starts only at v0.8.0 (confirmed by hand-walk: v0.7.0's `## [0.7.0]` section goes straight to `### Added` with no banner line, while v0.8.0's `## [0.8.0]` section opens with `**Minor release** (`methodology/06_release_train.md` §3.2)`), so class (iii) applies UNIFORMLY across all ten value-drift tags regardless of which of class (i)/(ii) each also carries. Confirmed per-tag disposition, full 14-tag sweep, CORRECTED (round-4 revision, fixing BLOCKER finding I9 and MAJOR finding I10): v0.8.0, v0.9.0, v1.0.0 hand-walk to a clean `--mode tag` exit 0 -- v0.8.0 with a group-5 pre-convention ROADMAP-disposition skip label present (rule (b)); v0.9.0/v1.0.0 with zero skips. v0.1.0 does NOT hand-walk to exit 0 (correcting the round-2/round-3 assumption that absence-skip alone made it clean): group 2 (docs/guide/index.html) and group 5 (docs/planning/ROADMAP.md) correctly SKIP on file-level absence (rule (a), unchanged), but groups 1, 3, and 4 correctly emit a named FAIL under the sub-anchor-absence rule ((a)-extension above) -- group 1 because CONTEXT.md is present at v0.1.0 but carries no `change_log` key (`git show v0.1.0:CONTEXT.md | grep change_log` returns no match), group 3 because README.md is present at v0.1.0 but carries none of the four version pins (curl URL / GOVERNANCE_TAG / --tag / releases-tag; `git show v0.1.0:README.md` contains no such pin), and group 4 because CHANGELOG.md's `## [0.1.0]` section is present at v0.1.0 but opens directly with `### Added`, carrying no tier-banner line (the `**Major release**` / `**Minor release**` / `**Patch release**` convention begins only at v0.8.0, confirmed by the same v0.7.0-vs-v0.8.0 hand-walk cited above) -- so `--mode tag --tag v0.1.0` correctly hand-walks to exit 1, and v0.1.0 joins the intentionally-blocked list under its OWN distinct cause, PRE-CONVENTION (none of classes (i)/(ii)/(iii), since v0.1.0 carries no NIZAM.json/CONTEXT.md value drift at all -- it is the tag every later drift is measured FROM). v0.2.0 hand-walks to exit 1 (groups 2 and 5 correctly SKIP on absence, but additions (b)/(c) correctly FAIL on the genuine 0.2.0-tag-vs-0.1.0-anchor value mismatch -- class (i) -- AND group 4 correctly FAILs on the tier-banner sub-anchor-absence -- class (iii), NOT an era-safety gap either way); v0.6.0 hand-walks to exit 1 (group 5 correctly SKIPs on absence, but PR-mode group 1 correctly FAILS on the genuine CONTEXT.md 0.5.0-vs-0.6.0 value mismatch -- class (ii) -- AND group 4 correctly FAILs on class (iii), also NOT an era-safety gap); v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.7.0 all carry the same class-(ii) CONTEXT.md mismatch PLUS class (iii) and hand-walk to exit 1 for the identical, correct reasons; v0.5.2/v0.5.3 additionally carry class (i) PLUS class (iii). The accurate, evidence-anchored claim this contract makes is therefore NARROWER than 'dispatch republication works for all 14 existing tags' and NARROWER than the round-2/round-3 'crash-free and false-FAIL-free for every absence-class historical gap' framing: rules (a)/(b) make `--mode tag` crash-free for every FILE-LEVEL-absence gap (rule (a)) and every ROADMAP pre-convention disposition gap (rule (b)) across all 14 tags (verified) -- that is the full and only scope of what rules (a)/(b) themselves cover; the sub-anchor-absence case (file present, expected anchor within it absent) is a separate, third mechanism (the (a)-extension) that is also crash-free, by construction, but is NOT false-FAIL-free and is not meant to be -- it deliberately and correctly emits a named FAIL, exactly at v0.1.0 across all three of its present-but-incomplete anchors in this 14-tag sweep (plus, as class (iii), at the ten value-drift tags' group 4). `--mode tag` exits 0 cleanly only where a tag's anchors are, in fact, internally value-consistent with each other, with the tag itself, AND fully populated per the then-current convention -- confirmed for v0.8.0, v0.9.0, v1.0.0 only (three historical tags, not four: v0.1.0 is excluded by its own genuine pre-convention FAILs). For the remaining tags carrying genuine pre-existing value drift and/or sub-anchor absence, `--mode tag` correctly continues to FAIL -- the check doing its job on real historical data, not a defect this contract's era-safety design is meant to, or should, suppress; non_goals already excludes any version-anchor repair as this feature's scope, and non_goals (round-4 revision) now states explicitly that dispatch republication of these ELEVEN specific tags -- v0.1.0 (pre-convention), v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.4.1, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.6.0, v0.7.0 (value drift plus tier-banner absence) -- is intentionally blocked by the tag-mode gate; repairing that historical drift or pre-convention gap (if ever desired) is a separate, future candidate outside this contract.
design_notes.roadmap_paths_filter_rationale: docs/planning/ROADMAP.md is added to release_closeout.yml's PR-mode paths filter (round-2 revision, fixing MINOR finding I8). PR-mode assertion group 5 reads ROADMAP.md's disposition line, so a pull request touching ONLY docs/planning/ROADMAP.md (e.g. a roadmap-only planning edit that inadvertently removes, duplicates, or mis-versions the 'Latest released tag' / 'Release in preparation' line) would previously never trigger the close-out gate at all, since the original five-path filter [CHANGELOG.md, NIZAM.json, CONTEXT.md, README.md, docs/guide/**] had no ROADMAP.md entry -- leaving the disposition-line invariant unenforced on exactly the PRs most likely to break it. This closes that hole without broadening assertion scope elsewhere: unlike the migration-link exclusion (migration_link_exclusion_rationale above, which deliberately narrows what group 3 ASSERTS because migration links legitimately stay pinned across no-new-migration MINOR releases), this fix broadens what TRIGGERS the gate, not what the gate asserts -- group 5's assertion logic (assertion_summary_pr_mode item 5) is unchanged; it simply now also runs on ROADMAP-only PRs, matching group 5's own read dependency on that file.

files_create.purpose: Stdlib-only, network-free close-out script (~170 lines) implementing require(label, condition), the five PR-mode assertion groups and three tag-mode additions from design_notes, with the round-2 tag-mode era-safety SKIP rules (anchor absence, ROADMAP disposition-label absence; see tag_mode_era_safety_design), argparse --mode {pr,tag} and --tag for tag mode; prints 'PASS <label>' per assertion, 'FAIL <label>' plus sys.exit(1) at the first failing assertion; contains no git-ref-mutating call of any kind.
